records.title: Laya: specialist performance is not base-model performance

protocol.split: Official test split reported by the author; specialist uses workflow training data
protocol.reference: Teacher-based synthetic benchmark references, not independent observed business outcomes
protocol.training: Specialist fine-tuned; base comparison is not fine-tuned on these workflows
protocol.measurement: Hard-label accuracy; calibration caveats separately reported
protocol.hardware: Not required for the accuracy statement; no latency claim imported

records.conclusion: The useful result is a within-project base-versus-specialist contrast, not evidence of universal superiority over Jev.
caveats: The Jev value on the source card is imported from another report with different prompts/sample sizes; excluded from this side-by-side measurement.
The released checkpoint discloses temperature fitting on a training slice and a conflicting inherited temperature configuration. Do not treat its current confidence as held-out calibrated.
A teacher-agreement reference is not an objective ceiling on real-world correctness.

artifacts.raw_outputs: Not independently audited by this list

records.title: CLM: a domain-trained selector recovers more successful supplied candidates

protocol.split: 75/38 task-disjoint training/evaluation split, seed 42; 66 training tasks have successful trajectories, split 59/7 for train/validation
protocol.reference: Trajectory pass outcomes as described by the release; environment execution not rerun here
protocol.training: A specialized projection head initialized from CLM v0.1-8B, not the generic checkpoint alone
protocol.measurement: Best-of-4; trajectory score averages final 12 available step scores
protocol.hardware: Accuracy claim only; candidate generation and full end-to-end cost not measured here

records.conclusion: This is selection improvement on a small, task-specific held-out set. It is not the coding success rate of a standalone 8B agent or a full official SWE benchmark score.
caveats: The candidate generator, sampling budget and candidate quality are part of the system.
38 tasks provide limited precision; paired per-task outcomes are needed for a defensible significance analysis.
Do not transfer results from this trained head to CLM zero-shot use.

records.title: Nimble vs Jev: paired human-reference comparisons remain task-dependent

protocol.task: 13 public-data subsets, including intent and sentence understanding
protocol.test_unit: 3,880 records overall; MASSIVE en-US example below has 350 records
protocol.split: Public subset manifests and family identifiers described in the pinned report
protocol.reference: Dataset human labels; some distributions are vote fractions rather than objective probabilities
protocol.training: Released nimble-9b vs Jev 1.13.0; provenance of all pretraining data is not fully known
protocol.measurement: Same record IDs and reference labels; no candidate shuffling; Nimble raw temperature 1.0

records.conclusion: This is a useful paired protocol, but a small difference in one subset does not establish a general winner.
caveats: The Nimble project ran the comparison; it is not an independent audit.
Manifests and procedures are public, while raw run/comparison outputs are gitignored and must be regenerated.
A subsequently fitted temperature was not applied to these reported runs; do not mix it with the displayed calibration numbers.
Records can share source families. Uncertainty analysis should account for clustering and multiple comparisons.

records.title: GLiNER2.5-Decide: keep a newly reported suite in its proper scope

protocol.test_unit: 17 domains × 300 held-out examples = 5,100 records, as reported
protocol.split: Author-described held-out split; independent dataset inspection incomplete
protocol.reference: Label provenance and benchmark construction not fully audited here
protocol.training: Checkpoint-specific models; training/test overlap not independently established
protocol.measurement: Average exact-match accuracy on an English suite

records.conclusion: The card supports including this family in local classification experiments, not declaring it universally better than Jev or Laya.
caveats: The accessible source is the 1B card, not an independently audited 340M release.
The table contains JevK5, not TypeSafe Jev.
The English suite cannot establish multilingual production quality.
A larger model does not automatically win this particular reported suite.

records.title: Kev: preserve development/test and source-domain distinctions

protocol.task: Typed decisions on the project’s new-source suite
protocol.test_unit: Dataset/sample definitions must be read with the pinned repository report
protocol.split: New-source development and held-out test are separate; trained-source results are a different slice
protocol.reference: Project benchmark references; not treated here as real-world outcome labels
protocol.training: Kev-4B release represented in the pinned README; model revisions can move independently of repository commits
protocol.measurement: New Sources accuracy reported as development / test

records.conclusion: The split distinction is more informative than copying a single score. This record is an archival source snapshot, not a claim about the latest downloaded weights.
caveats: Model selection on development results is not a blind final evaluation.
A pinned README commit fixes the source text, not the weights served by a live model ID.
Do not compare these numbers with a different task mix or a Jev result from another split.
